clues: This capital is the biggest city in the Baltic lands of north east Europe. Crowds know it best for the fine old town at its heart.
For much of the cold time of year, the lakes near town stay locked in ice. Even the rivers can freeze hard in the most cold winters here.
This town has been the seat of its land since the year 1323 at least. Grand Duke Gediminas named it as the chief town in a letter that year.
When Napoleon rode through in 1812, he gave this town a grand nick name. He called it the Jerusalem of the North, for it was a great home of Jewish life.
Its old town is one of the best kept old towns in all of Europe. The whole old town is kept safe as a world site of worth.
